description: RFC 6962 §2.1.2 consistency-proof vectors for Tzun growing logs. Tree math is the RFC 6962 tree profile (Tree): leaves are the RAW 32 bytes of a digest, leafHash = SHA-256(0x00 || d), node = SHA-256(0x01 || left || right), MTH splits at the largest power of two strictly less than n. A proof is PROOF(m, D[n]) = SUBPROOF(m, D[n], true), as bare lowercase hex, innermost element first. Verification is RFC 9162 §2.1.4.2 with the edge rules of Tree §3.5.
source: Computed by scripts/generate-consistency-vectors.mjs, a from-scratch RECURSIVE transcription of RFC 6962 §2.1.2 SUBPROOF that imports nothing but node:crypto. Every valid entry was verified, every invalid entry refused, and every encoding entry given its stated outcome by the script's own transcription of RFC 9162 §2.1.4.2 before being written. The engine implementation these vectors pin (packages/engine/src/merkle.ts) is iterative and walks node indices. scripts/regenerate-vectors.ts does not and must not rewrite this file.

format.leafDigests: The 64 leaf digests of one log. A tree of size n is leafDigests[0:n]. leafDigests[i] = sha256(utf8("tzun-merkle-vector-" + i)), the same leaves as merkle-rfc6962-vectors.json.
format.valid: Each entry is a verifier input {first, second, firstRoot, secondRoot, proof} that MUST verify. proof is exactly PROOF(first, leafDigests[0:second]); a generator MUST reproduce it byte for byte. Every pair 0 < first <= second <= 16, plus selected pairs up to 64.
format.invalid: Each entry is a verifier input {first, second, firstRoot, secondRoot, proof} that MUST NOT verify. mutation says what was changed; derivedFrom names the honest (first, second) it came from. The mutations are applied to every valid pair with second <= 8 and to a listed set of larger pairs, and first = 0 and first > second are added on their own.
format.encoding: Each entry is a verifier input {first, second, firstRoot, secondRoot, proof} with its expected outcome in verifies. They pin the encoding rule in edgeRules; the math around them is the honest (3, 7) proof or (5, 5). proof elements here may be any JSON value, not only strings.
format.sizeMalleability: Documentation, not conformance. Honest proofs that ALSO verify under a different claimed size, under any RFC-correct verifier. See its note.

edgeRules: first must satisfy 0 < first <= second. first = 0 is refused, including with an empty proof and including first = second = 0: Tzun never publishes an empty log. transparency-dev/merkle v0.0.2 accepts exactly those cases (five entries in invalid: the four "first = 0 with an empty proof" and "first = 0 and second = 0"); its main branch (v0.0.3-0.20260921095310-fbbcd741c3d1) refuses every entry in invalid.
first == second verifies only with an empty proof and firstRoot == secondRoot.
first < second with an empty proof is refused.

Every hash (each proof element, firstRoot and secondRoot) is a JSON string of exactly 64 hexadecimal digits, matched against the whole string. Uppercase and mixed case are accepted and normalised to lowercase before hashing and comparison. Anything else is refused: a trailing newline, surrounding whitespace, 63 or 65 digits, a 0x prefix, or a non-string. A regular expression must be anchored to the whole string: in Python use re.fullmatch, because re.match with $ also matches before a trailing newline.

sizeMalleability.note: Neither an inclusion proof nor a consistency proof authenticates the tree size it was made for. A verifier recomputes a root from the path and the claimed size; when a different size gives the same sequence of left and right steps, the computation is identical and the proof verifies. No verifier can reject those sizes from the proof alone. So every verifier takes the size as an explicit input, and the size must come from an authenticated checkpoint. The census counts, over every honest proof with second size <= 64, the proofs that also verify under at least one other claimed second size <= 64 (inclusion: leafIndex fixed; consistency: first fixed, both roots unchanged), and the consistency proofs that verify under another claimed FIRST size (second and both roots unchanged).
